figure_legends.before:
\section*{Figure legends}
\paragraph{Figure 1.} A selected Treasury-bill path that returns within the reported historical limit at its endpoint after an intervening breach. The rule chooses the earliest eligible original evaluation window. Endpoint containment can conceal a peak breach.

\paragraph{Figure 2.} Saved short-horizon FX learning curves on the original evaluation period. The methods retain distinct original penalty menus, and every tested history is shown against its own matched historical headroom. This retrospective comparison does not identify a universally optimal history.

\paragraph{Figure 3.} Expanded-menu regression relative loss versus matched historical headroom for every eligible CFTC contract. Columns separate histories; code order follows the fixed open-interest ranking. Positive values mean higher regression loss.

\paragraph{Figure 4.} Signed decomposition of regression excess loss against matched historical headroom, with selection in blue, the finite-menu diagnostic gap in orange, and actual excess as black dots. Crosses retain unavailable comparisons; the text focuses on short-history weekly cells while all planned comparisons remain plotted.

\paragraph{Figure 5.} Fixed reserve and breach-charge regions with the exceedance coefficient held at unity. Color shows the fraction of related comparisons where the stated conditional procedure costs less than corrected historical headroom, with each source group retaining its own histories and horizons. These are descriptive fractions; all comparisons are complete, and the lower and upper fractions coincide.
